newsitem.title: USA: Texaco says too early to assess refinery fire.
newsitem.headline: Texaco says too early to assess refinery fire.

text.p: Texaco Inc said on Monday it was too early to tell how a morning fire would affect production at its 96,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery in Wilmington, Calif.
"At this point, it's really too early to speculate on what impact it would have," said Kelly McAndrew, a company spokeswoman.
She said the refinery ran at reduced rate, but could not specify the amount of the cutback or how long it would last.
The cause of the fire remains under invesitigation, fire officials said earlier. They said the blaze began around 0720 PST/1520 GMT and was extinguished by 0830 PST/1630 GMT.
Texaco said the fire began in one of the refinery's four hydrotreaters.
Fire officials said it would take several hours before the damaged area was cool enough for investigators to enter.
"We don't know if its a simple repair or major," Texaco's McAndrew said.

Wholesale prices for Los Angeles gasoline and diesel began to rise after news of the fire. Bids for conventional regular gasoline rose one cent to 59 cents a gallon, while ultra-clean CARB gasoline saw a rise of 0.75 cent to 63 cents a gallon.
Brokers speculated the plant could lose at least 20,000 bpd of gasoline production.
"That seems like pretty high speculation," the Texaco spokeswoman said, when asked about the figure.
